title: How to Get Around China as a Tourist (2026): Trains, Metro & Apps
description:
Getting around China in 2026 is easier than almost anywhere you've traveled — once you set it up in the right order. This is the full, up-to-date guide to moving around China as a foreign tourist: high-speed trains between cities, spotless cheap metros within them, DiDi for taxis without a word of Mandarin, the 8-minute Maglev airport trick, and the exact apps to install before you fly.

Chapters:
0:00 Intro: the $7 airport train
0:29 Why China is easier than you think
1:01 High-speed trains: the backbone
2:43 City metros: cheap and easy
3:50 DiDi: taxis without the language barrier
4:36 The Maglev airport trick
5:28 The apps to set up before you fly
6:21 Get online before you land
7:11 Where the fast trains don't reach
7:43 Bonus tip + final checklist

Quick reference:
• High-speed rail: 50,000+ km network, up to 350 km/h, 50+ cities. Book on the 12306 app or Trip.com (English, foreign cards). Ride second class.
• Metro: distance-based fares from ~¥3; Shanghai Metro takes tapped Visa/Mastercard contactless (since 2025). English signage everywhere.
• DiDi: China's ride app, runs in English, takes overseas cards, sends your destination to the driver in Chinese.
• Shanghai Maglev: Pudong Airport ↔ Longyang Road, ~¥50 (~$7), 8 minutes at up to 430 km/h.
• Set up before you fly: a travel eSIM (get online past the firewall), Alipay/WeChat Pay, DiDi, 12306/Trip.com, and an offline map.

Prices and rules were checked in September 2026; fares and policies change, so confirm the specifics before you travel. This is general travel information, not visa or legal advice — always check official sources for entry requirements.

Sources: chinafortravelers.com · shanghaitourism.org · trip.com · travelchinaguide.com · en.wikipedia.org (Rail transport in China)
